why_it_made_the_list: Highest KPI score at 12/13. 3M likes. DeoDap Rs 159/188g, 4.81 from 100 reviews. No competitor price anchor.
claude_pick_reason: MY PICK, and the only one of the six that survives the marketplace check. On Meesho these sell from Rs 127 to Rs 1,604 with a median of Rs 543, so our Rs 1,299 sits INSIDE the range buyers already see - we are at the premium end of a known market, not outside it. That is the difference between this and every other row here. Its ad market is also unanchored: ~6 advertisers, none older than 4 months. Beats C018 (8 competitors fixed it at Rs 399), C019 and C017 (6.7x and 8.0x over their marketplace medians), and C021 (Meesho sells it at roughly our supplier cost). Weaknesses, stated plainly: only 4 months of ad history, so demand is proven and profitability is not, and it is motorised, so some units will fail and we sell no warranty.

why_it_made_the_list: Found by searching ads at our price point rather than viral Reels. First product where our price sits INSIDE what competitors already charge instead of above it.
claude_pick_reason: STRONGEST NEW FIND and the first candidate we could sell at the market price rather than above it. 14 distinct advertisers charge Rs 699-1,199, median Rs 999; DeoDap supplies it at Rs 199 for 370g, rated 4.39 from 142 reviews. Selling at Rs 999 puts us exactly at the median - no price objection to overcome, which is the problem that blocked C018, C019 and the sewing machine. Break-even CPP Rs 407 and target Rs 285 against a real CPP of Rs 200-250. Ranked just under C016 only because the oldest ad is 6 months against C016's open pricing field, and because it is motorised with implied wellness benefits we must not overclaim.

verdict: LIVE CANDIDATE. Priced at the market median, not above it. Do not make medical claims.

why_it_made_the_list: Only candidate clearly passing KPI 9 (saves the buyer money) - replaces a repeat purchase.
claude_pick_reason: REINSTATED - my Gate 4 was wrong and the owner called it. I blocked this for being 8x the Meesho median, but Meesho is the bargain end of the Indian market and our buyer is impulse-buying from a Reel, not running a price comparison. Pricing above Meesho is the business model, not a defect. Unlike the masala box, a silicone stretch lid is not something most buyers have owned, so no fixed price sits in their head. It keeps the best KPI-9 story we have: it replaces cling film, a repeat purchase. Two genuine reservations remain, neither of them the price multiple: the DeoDap rating is 3.91 from 35 reviews, the weakest of any match and a real RTO risk on COD, and its ad market has still not been checked, so we do not know whether competitors have anchored it the way they anchored C018.
verdict: REINSTATED under the corrected Gate 4. Live candidate, second priority.

why_it_made_the_list: Only category found where Indian dropshippers routinely advertise well above Rs 2,000.
claude_pick_reason: Proof that high-ticket dropshipping works in India: 9 advertisers charging Rs 999-6,999, median Rs 2,399. DeoDap supplies at Rs 1,059 so selling at the Rs 2,399 median gives target CPP Rs 395 even after assuming a punishing 45% RTO. Ranked fourth on risk, not economics: Rs 1,059 of stock rides on every parcel against a Rs 15,000 cap, it weighs 962g so returns are expensive, and a high-value COD parcel is the easiest kind to refuse at the door. A product for after a cheaper winner is funding us.

why_it_made_the_list: Best ad proof in the dataset. Retained as the worked example of why proof alone is not enough.
claude_pick_reason: Not recommended, and it is the most instructive failure here. It has the best evidence of anything we found - 8 separate dropshippers, one advertising continuously for 13 months - and that is exactly why it cannot be used. All 8 sell it at Rs 399 with free shipping and COD. Our break-even CPP at Rs 399 is Rs 78 against a real Indian CPP of Rs 200-250, so it loses money at the market price, and the only price where it earns is 2.75x what buyers are already being shown for the identical item. Revisit only with real differentiation: a bundle nobody else sells, or a segment the Rs 399 sellers are not reaching.
ad_advertisers_named: Home And Kitchen SW 3; Home & Kitchen SW; DealMate; Home & Kitchen U4 P2; Home And Kitchen 2 SW; Home & Kitchen U3 P2; Premium Store; Home & Kitchen 6 SW
verdict: BLOCKED ON PRICE ANCHOR. Fails the undercut test.

why_it_made_the_list: Cheapest supply at Rs 74 and best-reviewed match found. Everyday Indian kitchen item, squarely on the target demographic.
claude_pick_reason: Blocked, and the owner agrees: a masala box is a very common object and buyers know roughly what it should cost. That recognisability is the block, NOT the Meesho multiple - my first version of this gate used the multiple and that was wrong. The economics confirm it independently: at a credible Rs 499 our break-even CPP is Rs 174, below the real Indian CPP of Rs 200-250, so it loses money at any price a buyer would accept.
market_inside_range: NO (and item is a recognisable commodity - this is the block)
verdict: BLOCKED ON PERCEIVED VALUE. Meesho median Rs 180; our Rs 1,199 is 6.7x. Squeezed: credible price loses money.

why_it_made_the_list: 35K likes. Largest absolute margin per order of any candidate once priced correctly.
claude_pick_reason: Blocked, but for a measured reason rather than my earlier wrong one. I first rejected it for costing Rs 911 'against our Rs 1,099 price', which was a mistake - Rs 1,099 is a floor, not a price. The real problem only showed up on Meesho: sellers there list it between Rs 796 and Rs 977, clustered tightly around Rs 924. That is essentially our supplier cost of Rs 911. We cannot buy it for what they sell it for, so at market price we are underwater before a rupee of advertising. Our Rs 2,499 plan is 2.5x above the dearest listing on the platform. Unlike C016, whose price sits inside the observed range, this one sits far outside it.
verdict: BLOCKED. Meesho sells this at ~Rs 924, essentially our Rs 911 supplier cost.
